# Generated 2026-11-16. Current version: 0.5.16 (ARM64 Android only).

## What StoryCam is

StoryCam is a free Android app that records the front and back cameras at
the same time into one portrait video. The place fills the screen and you
are in a circle in the corner, reacting to it live. What you see on screen
is exactly what gets saved. It is built for travel vlogs, reaction videos,
and family videos: one take, one video, no editing needed.

StoryCam is the example app of the Dual Cameras open-source Flutter plugin
by Roman Slack. The plugin records the front and back cameras together on
Android and iOS, compositing them live on the GPU into a single portrait
MP4 and photo, in picture-in-picture, circle, or split layouts.

## Price

Free. No account, no ads, no watermark, no in-app purchase. Price is 0 USD.

## Status

Current version: 0.5.16 (ARM64 Android only). In testing on Google Play
(internal track). The free APK is also on GitHub:
https://github.com/dzianisv/dual_cameras/releases/latest
The newest APK is always at https://dzianisv.github.io/dual_cameras/latest.html

## Features

- Simultaneous front and back camera recording into one portrait video
- Picture-in-picture, circle inset, and split layouts; live swap of the
  main lens
- Lens pills from the camera API: front 1x/1.5x, rear 0.5x/1x where the
  phone supports it
- Live map in the corner while you record: it moves with you and rotates
  with the compass; pinch to zoom; place name shown; the map is burned
  into the recorded video
- Live filters and exposure controls, including game-look filters
  Vice City and San Andreas, plus Hyper, Midnight, Simple, Jakarta
- On-device captions in Russian and English (Whisper speech model):
  automatic language detection, or force Auto / Русский / English;
  karaoke-style highlighting follows the words as they are spoken
- Silence stays silent: captions only appear where speech is detected
  (Silero VAD)
- The original video is always kept; the captioned copy is saved to
  the gallery
- Model download and captioning run as system notifications with a
  progress bar and a Stop button
- Last-video thumbnail with Open / Delete / Share
- In-app review prompt after a successful recording (Play In-App Review API)

## How captions work

Captions run entirely on the phone with the Whisper speech model — no
audio is uploaded. The first time you turn captions on, the app downloads
about 160 MB of caption models, verified before they are trusted. After
that, recording, transcription, and burn-in all happen on-device. Single
short words are the hardest case for automatic language detection, so
force a language for short clips.

## Requirements

StoryCam needs an ARM64 Android phone with concurrent front-and-back
camera support, for example Pixel 6 and newer or Galaxy S22 and newer.
If the phone cannot run both cameras at once, the app falls back to
single-camera recording. Concurrent capture is capped at about 720p by
the camera system.

## Privacy

No account. No cloud. Captions are transcribed on-device and nothing is
uploaded. Videos stay on the phone. Privacy policy:
https://dzianisv.github.io/dual_cameras/privacy.html

## FAQ

Q: Is StoryCam on Google Play?
A: StoryCam is in testing on Google Play now (internal track, version
0.5.16). Until the public listing goes live, the free APK is on GitHub:
download it, allow install from unknown sources when prompted, and open it.

Q: How do Russian captions work in StoryCam?
A: Captions run entirely on the phone with the Whisper speech model — no
audio is uploaded. The first time you turn captions on, the app downloads
about 160 MB of caption models. You can leave the language on Auto or force
Русский or English. Single short words are the hardest case for automatic
detection, so force a language for short clips.

Q: Which phones does StoryCam work on?
A: StoryCam needs an ARM64 Android phone with concurrent front-and-back
camera support, for example Pixel 6 and newer or Galaxy S22 and newer. If
the phone cannot run both cameras at once, the app falls back to
single-camera recording.

Q: Do my videos or audio leave the phone?
A: No. Captions are transcribed on-device, and nothing is uploaded. The
original video is always kept, and the captioned copy is saved next to it.

Q: How do I stop a model download or captioning in StoryCam?
A: Both run as system notifications with a progress bar and a Stop button.
Stopping a download aborts it (you can retry from the Captions sheet);
stopping captioning abandons the job and keeps your original video — no
captioned video is ever saved after a stop.

## Blog post: I went traveling and wanted to vlog for my family — so I built the camera app I needed

I was traveling, and I wanted to send my family and friends videos that
felt like being there with me. Not a photo dump, not a shaky clip of a
street — a video where they could see my face and the place at the same
time.

My phone made me choose. The camera app records the street, or the selfie
camera records me. Never both. If I filmed the place, my family never saw
my reaction. If I filmed myself, they never saw where I was. I could film
twice and edit them together, but I was on holiday, not in a studio, and
editing on a phone with tired fingers after a long day is not a holiday.

So I looked for a free camera app that records both cameras at once. The
paid ones wanted a subscription for a feature that should be a button.
The free ones were either abandoned, full of ads, or recorded the two
cameras as two separate files — which puts me right back at editing.
None of them did what I actually wanted: press record, talk to my family,
show them the place, stop, send.

StoryCam is a free Android app. You open it, you press record, and it
records both cameras at the same time into one portrait video: the place
fills the screen, and you are in a circle in the corner, reacting to it
live. What you see on screen is exactly what gets saved.

The camera opens by itself when you open the app. There is a small live
map in the corner that moves with you. The filter slider sits above the
record button — I use Vice City and San Andreas for a game look. After a
take, the last video sits as a thumbnail next to the record button: tap
it to watch it, share it, or delete it.

Captions are the part my family notices most. StoryCam writes what I say
straight into the video, on the phone, in Russian or English — no upload,
no account. My grandmother reads along in Russian while I talk. The words
light up as I say them, like karaoke.

The map is burned into the recorded video too, so the video itself shows
where it was shot.

It is free — no pay model at all. No subscription, no one-time unlock,
no ads. The app is in testing on Google Play now, and the APK is on
GitHub. If you travel and your family is far away, try it: open the app,
press record, and talk to them as if they were standing next to you.

Try StoryCam: https://dzianisv.github.io/dual_cameras/storycam.html
